records.reason: m13 at 1/1 provides a lower-strength point for a multifunctional acceptor-rich scaffold. Its predicted V2 interval is broad; measured m13 rows c4bb286978fe9078a303 and ca467c94f14b2219503e show large endpoint shifts that make this point valuable for curve interpolation.

m125 at 1/1 and higher loading tests whether the large measured tail seen at 5/1 in 780b13846ace50ede763 and at 1/1 in f4fb5c03b8e8996e75f6 is condition- and loading-dependent rather than a fixed scaffold offset.
m117 at 20/1 extends a high-uncertainty multifunctional aldehyde condition beyond the measured 10/1 and 50/1 behavior in ea004678fc850c759752 and d9c8c8af50a10bf07765, targeting V2 curvature.

m160 at 5/1 with only 50 ul loading is a direct loading-response contrast to measured m160 rows fbf7711e24f45bf06d4f and b4e0e9dc92fca2c88b90. The very wide predicted V1/V2 ranges make it useful for separating amount effects from nitrogen chemistry.

m161 supplies a positional isomer and a higher-volume 2/1 condition for the amino-nitrile family. It can test whether the observed m161 behavior in 5258960e057b56ed51f8 and 53a1acff30433cff819f transfers across loading and substitution.

m216 at 10/1 and 50 ul creates a same-ratio loading contrast to measured 10/1 at 150 ul in 222a68fc192f66c1c080 and to the lower-ratio point 5097ef8f92148f920ca4. Its broad V2 forecast targets a potentially nonlinear high-retention response.

m205 at 2/1 and 150 ul bridges the measured lower-loading and higher-ratio behavior in c973d4c257be9ef08216 and e8f592c469b2f3c136d8, testing whether loading and solvent strength jointly control the broad endpoint interval.

m206 at 5/1 and 150 ul extends the measured m206 series from b0f83f107759037eea65, 13bfaf03c35b4cff3bd5, and 614873124b33029a924c. This is a useful high-retention loading/condition interpolation point.
m135 at 10/1 and 100 ul tests whether the measured donor-scaffold shifts in f9f0f4e29dbd30c000ee and d05a91dc8e32e9edd7d persist at lower loading, with a wide predicted V2 range.

m114 at 50/1 and 100 ul adds a late condition below the measured 50/1, 150 ul row 0cf0d36290765378ae8d. It isolates amount dependence in an aromatic carbonyl scaffold with a large predicted completion interval.
m191 at 5/1 fills a condition gap between its measured low-ratio and higher-ratio aldehyde behavior, including the broad V2 responses in b0802294da4fd71d0f9d and bae9d67e095423d8edd2.

m198 at 20/1 and 50 ul probes the high-ratio tail of a nitro aldehyde scaffold. It complements the measured 50/1 point 8ab554cd154e9749790b and tests whether completion grows smoothly or changes sharply.

m211 at 50/1 and low loading targets an extreme predicted tail for a pyridyl-biphenyl scaffold. It extends the measured lower-ratio points such as 9fb05d784e7952bd4741 and can reveal high-ratio extrapolation failure.
m90 at 10/1 and 150 ul tests loading transfer against the measured 10/1, 100 ul high-retention example 96710afeabc594baa359 and the 5/1 example 29db30571b2a1ae59cc7.

m37 at 20/1 and 50 ul explores a high-uncertainty nitro-acetophenone condition, adding a late solvent point where the model predicts a much wider completion interval than its ordinary aromatic-carbonyl baseline.
m94 at 20/1 extends the measured multi-carbonyl response from 852d4f3443a81d662552 and 5b445b457a8b897a2d6. The high predicted V2 makes it informative for endpoint-specific tail calibration.
m107 at 5/1 and 150 ul is a loading contrast to measured 2/1 and 5/1 rows f96cee9775323fbf1d8b and d1172a49fca1e196a59f, both of which show that this ether-rich scaffold can have a large V2 response.

m119 at 2/1 and 100 ul fills a loading/ratio gap between measured m119 rows c32caf65e93924aeb179 and e6e78489d1da4066c07e. The prediction is broad enough to discriminate smooth interpolation from a scaffold threshold.

m73 at 50/1 tests the unusual same-scaffold response suggested by the measured low-ratio row 3d5a3094cb10eee37b37 and the 10/1 row 122a83bd31e4c0efeebd. It directly probes nonmonotonic or sharply curved solvent response.

m42 at 50/1 provides a late neutral-ketone anchor against the early measured row d7940150bb93b1b6bbb6 and the late measured row 1d9eabd939a185c1b128, constraining transfer across ordinary aromatic carbonyls.

m200 at 2/1 and 50 ul tests loading sensitivity in a nitro-phenethyl alcohol scaffold, complementing measured 0/1 and 1/1 observations such as 7dace1dbecce79e17117 and 3fbf4a3d05e84138e1e2.

m209 at 50/1 extends donor-containing phenol chemistry into a late solvent regime. The high predicted V2 width makes it a useful test of whether donor effects remain scaffold-specific after the recent polar-scaffold failures.
m204 at 5/1 and lower loading bridges the measured early condition 09b1bb29e7a0e3565a0d and the 2/1 condition 6a39aff909ea35989c74, testing donor-specific solvent and loading response.

m92 in EA at 10/1 adds a rare solvent/condition tuple and extends the measured EA points 10a4c811b70ba8155044 and e2f15590b7142490599b. This helps separate mobile-phase identity effects from generic carbonyl polarity.
m216 at 5/1 and 50 ul complements the selected 10/1 low-volume point, forming a meaningful within-molecule solvent curve while the measured 222a68fc192f66c1c080 anchors the high-volume response.

m116 at 50/1 and 100 ul tests loading interpolation against the measured late-ratio, higher-volume row 22300151ccec3f1f1c24 and the 20/1 row 9de8edaa330ab971f479, which show substantial late retention.

This molecule-novel chlorotoluene-like anchor adds weakly polar baseline chemistry at an early condition. It constrains aromatic/halogen transfer before applying corrections learned from high-retention polar scaffolds.
This molecule-novel dimethyl aromatic aldehyde provides a moderate-polarity carbonyl anchor with a broad V2 forecast, testing whether aldehyde corrections transfer beyond the measured families.
This molecule-novel halogenated aryl ether is a weakly polar condition anchor. Measuring it helps prevent high-retention polar corrections from distorting neutral aromatic and halogen transfer.

This molecule-novel chlorinated aromatic ester adds an intermediate-to-late neutral anchor with a distinct loading solvent and condition tuple, improving baseline calibration across the Row-distribution.

hypotheses.content: Large V2 errors concentrate in multifunctional, strongly hydrogen-bonding, or conjugated scaffolds and are endpoint-specific; a global retention correction is inadequate.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: V2 dominates several of the largest catalog errors. Labels in these regions can teach the model to represent completion separately from onset and to condition tail behavior on scaffold chemistry.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do high predicted V2 widths resolve into smooth scaffold-specific curves, or do particular functional-group arrangements create abrupt endpoint transitions?

hypotheses.content: Nitrogen-rich and donor-containing structures have scaffold- and loading-dependent solvent responses; generic polarity features do not determine their V1/V2 shifts.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The selected loading contrasts can distinguish amount effects from nitrogen or donor identity and improve transfer to underrepresented high-retention rows.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: At matched PE/EA ratio, does changing loading amount shift onset and completion together, or mainly broaden and delay V2?

hypotheses.content: PE/EA response is nonlinear and endpoint-specific for several scaffolds, with possible sharp transitions and condition/loading interactions.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Same-molecule condition curves give the retrained model direct information about solvent slopes and curvature, reducing extrapolation from sparse condition coverage.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Are the observed large ratio effects reproducible within a scaffold after loading is controlled, or do they reflect separate amount and solvent interactions?

hypotheses.content: Molecule-novel weakly polar anchors and rare condition tuples are needed to calibrate neutral aromatic transfer and prevent corrections from polar failure regions from propagating broadly.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Neutral and weakly polar rows form a large part of the Row-distribution. Novel anchors constrain the baseline representation while the targeted tail rows repair known failure regions.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do new neutral anchors reduce structural overcorrection when the model predicts nearby polar or multifunctional molecules?

feedback_interpretation: Recent measurements strengthened the case for scaffold-conditioned tail repair. The m207 series changed from 4.51/8.90 at low ratio in 3a69b15dc3ddae32533c to 45.38/72.03 at 10/1 in a19f98569910dc7fd6c4, showing that condition response can be abrupt. Large completion errors also persisted for m160 in b4e0e9dc92fca2c88b90, m66 in 49201b5817f204116f7f, m90 in 96710afeabc594baa359, m114 in 0cf0d36290765378ae8d, and m177 in 5e276c1730fc0a9deba7 and 4862e2fb71344ce16021. The m177 pair further showed that loading and solvent effects can interact rather than produce a universal shift. I therefore moved emphasis toward high-V2 and high-width condition/loading contrasts around multifunctional, nitrogen-rich, donor-bearing, and conjugated scaffolds, while retaining four molecule-novel weakly polar anchors for baseline transfer.
batch_rationale: The batch concentrates labels where the current predictor has shown its most consequential failures: broad predicted V2 intervals, multifunctional carbonyls, nitrogen-rich and donor-bearing scaffolds, and high-ratio extrapolation. Several selections form local response experiments, including m216, m125, m160, m161, m205, m206, m117, m119, m73, and m116, while others test loading at a fixed or nearby ratio. The final molecule-novel chlorotoluene, aldehyde, aryl ether, and chlorinated ester anchors constrain neutral structural transfer. Together these labels should improve endpoint-specific solvent representations, loading interactions, and calibration across both the high-retention tail and the much larger neutral portion of the Row-distribution.
